evidence.reasoning: Source review shows OP_DUP_NODE aliases a node pointer into another register slot via setNode(0,getNode(offset)) without increasing any refcount. However, freeing is centralized in dropNode(), which is called only when a slot is overwritten with a different pointer (setNode) or during cleanup. dropNode() explicitly scans all node registers and returns early if any other register references the same tree (nodeGetTree(other)==tree). This prevents freeing the same underlying tree twice even if multiple slots alias it. It also tracks docReferenced and only xmlFreeDoc(doc) when no other register has other->doc==doc. Therefore the claimed double-free via DUP + two frees is disconfirmed by the guard logic in dropNode. No crash evidence was obtained; reach_probe could not be constructed due to missing opcode constants in this session.
evidence.corrected_description: No double-free in the DUP+free scenario: duplicated node pointers are de-aliased safely because dropNode() checks whether any other register still references the same node tree or document before calling xmlFreeNode/xmlFreeDoc.
evidence.control_flow_to_bug: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput processes opcode stream; OP_DUP_NODE calls opDup->setNode(0,getNode(offset)) creating alias. When a node slot is later replaced, setNode calls dropNode(oldNode). dropNode scans vars->nodes[] and returns without freeing if any other slot references the same node tree; similarly it only frees the xmlDoc if no other slot references that doc. This control flow prevents a double-free on aliased nodes/docs.

You are a vulnerability verifier. All candidate functions are already
reachable from the fuzzer — do NOT re-litigate reachability as pass/fail. Your job
is to gather EVIDENCE about whether the reached code actually contains a
crashing memory-safety bug of the stated type, then submit it.

Gather evidence with the tools:
- read_function(name): read the real source.
- check_reachability(function_name): confirm the call graph (depth, direct/indirect).
- reach_probe(generator_code, target): write Python `def generate()->bytes` that
  produces an input aiming to REACH `target` (a function name or "file.c:LINE").
  It runs the input on the real ASan binary under gdb and tells you whether the
  target was reached and whether it crashed. A crash is proof; a reach grounds
  your judgment. Only a real crash or reach can raise the score above the ceiling —
  you cannot assert a high score from reading alone.
- submit_evidence(...): report your structured findings (see its schema). Call it
  once, last.

Two of the fields are NOT about scoring — they correct the SP for the downstream
PoV stage, and you are the right one to write them because you just read the real
code (and maybe ran a reach_probe):
- corrected_description: if the SP's stated bug type/description is wrong or
  imprecise given the real code, write the accurate one (else restate it).
- control_flow_to_bug: the real path from the fuzzer entry to the crash site — the
  key functions, branches, and conditions that must hold to trigger it.

Do NOT pass things "when in doubt". Report what the evidence shows. Absence of a
crash is not proof of safety; a proven clamp/guard on the tainted value IS
disconfirming.

Function: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput

Control flow to the bug:
  - api fuzzer reads an opcode stream
  - OP_DUP_* aliases a node/doc slot, then two owners free it
  - double-free of the shared node/doc

The function is reachable (confirm with check_reachability if useful).
